description: Fixed 3 bugs in the GSC reporting tool that each made it assert something false. Added getSiteTotals() (dimensionless GSC query), used in all 4 callers. Also rebuilt all ~90 historical snapshots from GSC and de-duplicated same-day entries (history had appended, not overwritten, so re-running /seo-check the same day compared today vs today and reported a flat 0%). (2) POSITION-BLIND CTR ADVICE: 'avgCtr < 1.0' compared a FRACTION (0.0019) to a percentage threshold, so '[HIGH] CTR should be 2-3%' fired unconditionally on every site every run. CTR is now judged against expected-CTR-for-position (new src/utils/ctr-curve.js), restricted to the top 20 where the curve is measurable. (3) HEALTH SCORE had no SEO signal in it: same fraction/percentage bug on the CTR factor (~0.016 of 25 points, always) and the position factor floored at 0 for any avg position >=20 (all 4 sites) — the score was GA4 engagement wearing an SEO label. Added src/striking-distance.js (queries + pages where clicks are actually available, split into snippet fixes vs ranking pushes).
reason: The changelog shows meta descriptions were rewritten 3 separate times (2026-05-18 mydojo x15, 2026-05-18 mytattoo x22, 2026-06-27 both) chasing a '[HIGH] CTR Optimization' recommendation that was firing unconditionally because of a units bug — on sites averaging position 30-40, where no snippet can earn a click. The tool was generating the work. Meanwhile every headline number and every historical trend it reported was inflated by a varying factor.

description: Sitemap <lastmod> across all 4 sites, derived honestly. petcare, mydojo and mytattoo emitted bare <loc> entries with no lastmod at all. driveschoolpro DID emit lastmod — but via serialize(item){item.lastmod = new Date().toISOString()}, which stamps every one of its 96 URLs with the BUILD TIME on every deploy. That asserts all 96 pages changed whenever you fix a typo, and Google's sitemap documentation is explicit that it ignores lastmod once it finds the values unreliable — so the dishonest version buys nothing and can burn the signal. Added scripts/sitemap-lastmod.mjs (shared by all 4 astro.config.mjs) which resolves a real per-page date in priority order: frontmatter updatedDate -> git last-commit date for the source file -> frontmatter date/pubDate -> filesystem mtime (reached only for files git has not seen yet) -> omit rather than invent. Added updatedDate to all 4 content collection schemas. Result: mydojo 34/34, mytattoo 39/39, petcare 48/48, driveschoolpro 96/96 URLs now carry dates that reflect actual edits, spread across real commit history rather than all sharing one timestamp.
reason: /seo-check 2026-07-28: 3 of 4 sites gave Google no freshness signal at all, and the 4th gave it a uniformly false one. lastmod is one of the few crawl-scheduling inputs available to a site with no authority — which matters most for petcare, the site getting ~0 crawls. Noting honestly that driveschoolpro (the only site that had any lastmod) also has 2.3x the crawl rate of its siblings: that is correlation, not established causation, and it is not the reason for the change — accuracy is.
expectedImpact: gives Googlebot a truthful recrawl signal per page; changed pages become distinguishable from unchanged ones, which the previous build-time approach made impossible
